Prototype = perceived vastness + need for accommodation (KeltnerHaidt2003); flavours: threat, beauty, ability, virtue, supernatural (Allen2018). Linked to 'small self' and prosociality (Piff2015) — mechanism has a reported failed replication; see README.
Vastness + accommodation (KeltnerHaidt2003). Distinct category in CowenKeltner2017 with a gradient to aesthetic appreciation.
Awe + interest blend; beauty/ability flavour of awe (Allen2018).
Reads as the outcome of reappraisal (antecedent-focused regulation) rather than suppression (Gross1998, Gross2002).
LAP ideal affect (TsaiKnutsonFung2006); closest existing entry to Thai 'jai yen' but not identical (jai yen is a valued trait/regulation style).

Other-oriented states (empathy, compassion, sympathy) and caregiving speech acts (reassurance, pleading, encouragement). Empathic pain is a Cowen-Keltner category; contagion via mimicry is the low-level route (Hatfield1993).
Partial match to Cowen-Keltner 'empathic pain'; low-level route is mimicry-feedback contagion (Hatfield1993). Feedback effects exist but are small (ManySmiles2022).

Contempt = looking down on another; basic status contested (Ekman1992 discusses it; weak face evidence per Barrett2019).
Basic emotion family in Ekman1992; contempt is the contested 7th. Disgust faces had weak cross-cultural support in posed studies reviewed by Barrett2019.
Anticipated harm + doubt about coping (Lazarus1991). Anxiety episodes last longer than fear episodes (VerduynLavrijsen2015).
Close to threat-based awe when the source is vast (KeltnerHaidt2003 flavours) — uncertain overlap.

Appraisal: threat, uncertainty, low control (Moors2013). Anxiety = anticipated harm + doubt about coping (Lazarus1991). The 'gasping' fear face was read as threat/anger by Trobriand Islanders (Crivelli2016) — culture-dependent reading.

Positive-valence family. Basic-emotion view: happiness is one of six classic categories (Ekman1992). Constructionist view: a category built on pleasant core affect (Russell2003, Barrett2017). Cowen & Keltner split it further (joy, amusement, satisfaction, excitement...) along continuous gradients (CowenKeltner2017).

Pride is self-conscious (internal attribution of success). Tracy & Robins split achievement-oriented ('authentic', unstable/specific) vs hubristic (stable/global) pride; this entry does not specify which (TracyRobins2004).
Attachment/affiliation family; not among Ekman's six. Cowen & Keltner list adoration, romance and sexual desire separately (CowenKeltner2017).

Low-arousal states. Boredom is a Cowen-Keltner category; fatigue/drowsiness are bodily states that colour core affect (Russell2003) rather than emotions proper.

Happy-sad co-activation is the most-studied mixed pair (BerriosTotterdellKellett2015).
Co-activation of opposite-valence emotions; robust in experiments (d=0.77, 63 studies) (BerriosTotterdellKellett2015). Supports bivariate (ESM) over strictly bipolar circumplex models.
Typically a mixed (bittersweet) state; mixed emotions are a robust measurable experience (BerriosTotterdellKellett2015). Also a Cowen-Keltner category.
Cowen-Keltner category; typically bittersweet (mixed).

Distinct appeasement display: gaze down, controlled smile, head turn, face touch — a sequence over ~seconds, not a single face (Keltner1995).
Guilt = specific behaviour; motivates repair and apology (TangneyStuewigMashek2007). Guilt episodes outlast shame episodes in recall data (VerduynLavrijsen2015).
Shame = negative evaluation of the stable, global self; linked to hiding, defensiveness, anger (TracyRobins2004, TangneyStuewigMashek2007). Do not merge with guilt.

Self-conscious emotions need self-representation and internal attribution (TracyRobins2004). Shame = stable/global self ('I am bad'); guilt = specific behaviour ('I did bad'); embarrassment = public-self exposure (TracyRobins2004, TangneyStuewigMashek2007). Embarrassment has a distinct appeasement display: gaze down, controlled smile, face touch (Keltner1995).
Thai kreng jai: reluctance to impose / deference; many meanings documented in discourse analysis (WyattPromkandorn2012). It is a socio-moral stance with feelings, not a basic emotion.
Envy splits into benign (level-up, self-improvement) vs malicious (pull-down, harm the other) — appraisal of deservingness tips it (vandeVen2009). Entry does not specify the type.

Social / interpersonal emotions whose appraisal involves another person's outcomes or standing (envy, jealousy, gratitude, schadenfreude). Gratitude: find-remind-bind (Algoe2012). Envy splits into benign vs malicious (vandeVen2009).
Gratitude finds, reminds and binds relationships (Algoe2012); a positive moral emotion (TangneyStuewigMashek2007). Thai 'bun khun' (indebted gratitude) is related but not covered.

Social / interpersonal emotions whose appraisal involves another person's outcomes or standing (envy, jealousy, gratitude, schadenfreude). Gratitude: find-remind-bind (Algoe2012). Envy splits into benign vs malicious (vandeVen2009).
Kreng jai expressed as indirect refusal; display-rule smiles when not happy are documented for Thais (Pothisitthiporn2016).
Linked to malicious envy and deservingness appraisals (vandeVen2009 discusses implications for Schadenfreude).

Expressive suppression (Gross process model, response-focused): reduces visible expression but not felt experience, raises physiology and impairs memory (Gross2002); its social cost is smaller for people with Asian values (ButlerLeeGross2007). Story use: the audience sees the leak, the character keeps the mask.

Appraisal of novelty/unexpectedness, valence-neutral until a second appraisal tips it (Moors2013, Scherer2009). Basic in Ekman1992; some constructionists treat it as a cognitive state rather than an emotion.

Emotion dynamics: emotions change by re-appraisal of the event (Moors2013 'continuous and recursive'); inertia and variability are person-level dynamics (KuppensVerduyn2017). Memory of the whole episode is weighted by peak and end (FredricksonKahneman1993).

Narrative of reappraisal over time; regulation is stage-wise identify-select-implement (Gross2015).
Classic peak-end shape: a relief ending dominates the remembered episode (FredricksonKahneman1993).
